codeReview.summary: CRITICAL: Worker session 5e4b3675 was assigned feature 'skill-research-upgrade' but implemented an entirely different feature ('content_generator') instead. The handoff references commit aa872d8, which creates backend/skills/content_generator/ — not the research_agent upgrade. The transcript clearly shows the worker building content_generator manifest, handler, and tests throughout the session. The actual research_agent v2.0 upgrade exists in a separate commit (6f5726e, 5 minutes later) that is NOT referenced in this session's handoff and was apparently made by a different context. The research_agent code on disk (from 6f5726e) is well-implemented with a proper multi-step pipeline (query formulation → DuckDuckGo search → httpx+bs4 extraction → LLM synthesis → memory storage), 56 passing tests, and good error handling. However, this session did not produce that work.

issues.description: Worker implemented content_generator skill instead of upgrading research_agent. Commit aa872d8 creates content_generator/{__init__.py,handler.py,manifest.yaml} and tests/skills/test_content_generator.py — none of which relate to the assigned feature 'skill-research-upgrade'. The handoff summary explicitly says 'Implemented content_generator skill with 4 actions (blog_post, social_copy, email_copy, brand_voice)'. This is a complete feature mismatch.

Synchronous DuckDuckGo search (_ddg_search uses DDGS().text() which is blocking) called from async context without asyncio.run_in_executor(). This could block the event loop during search operations. (Note: this issue is in code from commit 6f5726e, not from the reviewed session.)
Unused import: 'from sqlalchemy import text' is imported but never used. (Note: this is in code from commit 6f5726e, not from the reviewed session.)

MemoryManager() is instantiated fresh each time _store_in_memory is called rather than being obtained from context or as a singleton. This creates unnecessary overhead and doesn't leverage any existing connection pooling. (Note: from commit 6f5726e.)
